decision_description: For the MSCA-PF unit-cost, single-researcher instrument (selected_call.json: budget_regime='unit_cost', host_country='HU', project_duration_months=30), the budget gate (Phase 7 / gate_09) is declared 'pass' on the basis of the internal deterministic derivation (unit_cost_budget.json = confirmed_months x published_rates x host_country_coefficient, byte-equal replay-checked) as the sanctioned budget source, and NOT on the basis of an external Lump Sum Budget Planner response. It is determined that the emptiness of docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ (containing only .gitkeep, i.e. no external response) is out of scope for this instrument and is therefore NOT a blocking gate failure: the C1 amendment scopes 'absence of a received/ response is a blocking gate failure' to lump-sum instruments only. Every unit_cost_budget.json component, including the sole host-dependent line (living allowance, HU coefficient 78.7%), resolves to 'Confirmed', with unresolved_components=[] and blocking_inconsistencies=[]; total_eur=220723.5 remains solely within unit_cost_budget.json and is not materialized into the gate assessment.
alternatives_considered: Treat the empty lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ directory as a blocking budget-gate failure and halt before Phase 8 (rejected: C1 scopes the received/-absence blocking rule to lump-sum instruments only, so applying it to a unit-cost instrument would import a rule the constitution does not attach to this instrument).

Prepare and dispatch an external lump-sum budget request via the integration and await a validated received/ response before passing the gate (rejected: per CLAUDE.md §8.1 as amended by C1, lump-sum externalisation adds no anti-fabrication guarantee for a judgment-free unit-cost budget and would block the §2 programme-agnostic mission).

Materialize the derived numeric figures into budget_gate_assessment.json for convenience (rejected per §8.1/§8.3 anti-fabrication and figure-containment: numeric values remain solely within unit_cost_budget.json and are referenced only by filename).
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.4 (instrument-conditional budget-gate source; categorical Phase-8 block preserved and instrument-independent), read with §8.1 (unit-cost deterministic derivation is the sanctioned source, not an estimate) and the Section 8/7 C1 Constitutional Amendment Record (received/-absence blocking rule scoped to lump-sum instruments only)
rationale: The budget gate is instrument-conditional by source. MSCA-PF is a unit-cost, single-researcher instrument, so the sanctioned budget source is the internal deterministic derivation, byte-equal replay-checked, which supplies the anti-fabrication guarantee that externalisation supplies for lump-sum. The categorical §8.4 Phase-8 block is preserved and instrument-independent, and is satisfied here because every budget component — including the host-dependent living-allowance line — resolves to Confirmed with no unresolved components and no blocking inconsistencies. Structural consistency is assessed against the single-researcher work plan and host per §7 Phase 7: the fellowship unit costs fund the fellow at the host executing all five work packages, so the instrument carries no per-WP or per-partner budget lines and their absence is not-applicable rather than a coverage inconsistency. The empty received/ directory is documented explicitly rather than silently treated as passing, honouring §13.7/§13.8, and is not a blocking failure because C1 scopes that blocking rule to lump-sum instruments only.
